text:
Alex T: Heads-up — we've been seeing a pattern of Pending pods in eu-west1 when batches hit ~120 concurrent GPU requests. cluster-autoscaler claims no capacity in zone and doesn't trigger cross-zone provisioning. Anyone else noticed? :eyes:
Mari N: Yep. I traced it to quota + the autoscaler ignoring other zones because nodePools are zone-scoped and our autoscaler config has strict zoneAffinity. Logs show "no nodes available in zone" repeatedly.
Sam K: We have two levers: (1) relax zoneAffinity so CAS can provision in sibling zones, or (2) maintain a tiny warm pool of ephemeral GPU nodes per region to absorb spikes. Warm pool = cheaper than cold-starting a new nodetype under quota pressure.
Priya S: Warm pool sounds good but watch cost. Also cross-region provisioning will increase egress and latency for some customers. We should decide acceptable SLO tradeoffs if we route inference across regions.
Keegan L: Another option — use tainted warm nodes so only high-priority pods schedule there. Example k8s labels/taint:```yaml
nodeSelector:
  node.kubernetes.io/gpu: "true"
tolerations:
- key: "gpu-warm"
  operator: "Exists"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
```This keeps them reserved unless pods tolerate.
Alex T: Nice. How do we get autoscaler to create warm nodes automatically? Can we hook the autoscaler to a scheduled scaling policy (keep min=1 per region) or use a separate managed nodepool with minReplicas=1?
Mari N: We can create dedicated nodePools named gpu-warm-{region} with min=1, max=3. Set node taints as above and add a low-cost instance type (e.g., preemptible/spot) for most of the pool. Add a short eviction handler in the node-init to push metrics to infra-bot when preempted.
infra-bot: [alert] gpu-warm-eu-west1 node terminated (preempted) at 2026-06-12T09:03:21Z — re-provisioning attempt queued.
Sam K: Preemptible saves $$$ but expect churn. We should add fallback inference path: e.g., auto-switch to smaller model (8-bit quantized) in the API gateway if GPU capacity not available within N seconds. That will reduce immediate compute needs and is less disruptive than returning 503s.
Priya S: Agree. Also need routing rules in control-plane: prefer same-region, fallback to nearest-region with available capacity, then to quantized-model path. Must tag workloads with latency sensitivity so we don't route low-latency customers cross-region.
Keegan L: One wrinkle — our CNI and image pull rates caused pod startup delays during previous surge. Warm pool reduces image-pull concurrency, but we should also bake images into node images (or use a local registry mirror) to shave ~10-20s.
Alex T: Good call. Action items: (1) Mari — create gpu-warm nodepool templates per region (min=1, tainted, spot) and open PR with autoscaler settings. (2) Sam — prototype gateway fallback to quantized-model + timeout tuning (3s -> 1.5s grace for cross-region failover). (3) Priya — write runbook for routing decision matrix and egress-cost thresholds. I'll add an alert when Pending GPU pods > 10 for > 2m.
Mari N: I'll start the nodepool PR and include a sample cluster-autoscaler config and CA annotation to allow cross-zone provisioning. Sample snippet I'm planning to include:
```yaml
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--expander=least-waste
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
# permit scale out across zones
--node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled,k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/redwood
```
Priya S: Cool. Also add a note about network egress cost estimates in PR body. We don't want a surprise invoice if we start cross-region routing at scale.
Keegan L: I'll add a kubelet image-preload job to the warm nodes and test preempt handling.
Sam K: +1 on testing. We should run a chaos test where we kill warm nodes and verify fallback path within 30s.
Alex T: Great. Thanks all. Let's sync in infra sync on Friday to finalize SLOs for cross-region fallback. :thumbsup:
